text.p: Ashland Inc has budgeted fiscal 1997, ending September 30, capital spending of $525 million, chief executive Paul W. Chellgren said on Monday.
The company's spending totaled $510 million in 1996, Chief Financial Officier J. Marvin Quin said in remarks prepared for an analysts meeting in New York City.
"Last year at this meeting we told you we planned to invest two-thirds of our 1996 capital budget in our related energy and chemical businesses," other than Ashland Petroleum and SuperAmerica.
"In fact, we exceeded that goal," Quin said. "We invested nearly 72 percent, or $365 million, in these businesses."
Chellgren is prepared to tell the analysts that "Roughly two-thirds of the (1997) total, or $350 million, will be invested in our related energy and chemical businesses.

Noting the increase in Ashland Petroleum's budget, to $175 million this year from last year's $145 million, he said the largest projects are the continuing petrochemical and branded marketing expansions.

"Let me make it clear, however, that we intend to keep capital spending for Ashland Petroleum, excluding petrochemical and branded marketing expenditures, in line with or below annual depreciation levels."
Ashland expects "to fund our 19976 capital budget from internally generated funds," Chellgren said.
"In addition, while we will continue to seek attractive growth opportunities, we currently do not anticipate any material acquisitions in 1997."
